worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.summary: Temporarily make the chosen target Simple, doubling subsequent stat-stage gains and losses. An ally can be buffed or an enemy rewritten.
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.use.0: overwrite a foe's strong Ability with Simple
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.use.1: shut down a fighter that runs on its own Ability
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.use.2: give an ally Simple so its later boosts and drops are doubled
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.description: A Pokémon’s Ability becomes Simple for %1$s, doubling stat-stage changes. Abilities that cannot be overwritten, or are already Simple, are unaffected.
Beam range %1$s blocks, wind-up %2$s, recovery %3$s, following speed and size.
Wave radius %1$s blocks; the wave bursts at the target and washes over that area, wider on a wider body. It only sweeps non-allies.
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.wave.on: Psychic wave: bursts at the target and washes over a %1$s-block ring of non-allies, at %2$s cooldown and a shorter rewrite for each.
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.wave.off: Single beam: one target only, rewrite lasting %1$s, faster to cast.
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.timing: Range %1$s blocks, wind-up %2$s, recovery %3$s, %4$s PP, cooldown %5$s.
Wave mode affects nearby non-allies too, with duration ×0.6 and cooldown +18 ticks. Single beam affects only the target, with duration ×1.35 and cooldown −8 ticks.
The companion only considers a beam on a threat within this distance; lower stays close, higher chases further.
When on, it will leave its post to fire the beam.
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.growth.0: From level %1$s, cooldown is reduced by an extra 0.5 seconds.
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.growth.1: From level %1$s, the extra cooldown reduction becomes 1.1 seconds, replacing the earlier reduction.
world_combat.move.simplebeam.text.empty: The beam scatters into empty space; no target
worldcombat.skill.simplebeam.world: Non-Pokémon are affected for %1$s: subsequent stat-stage changes, including accuracy and evasion, are doubled within the usual ±6 limits. Both gains and losses are doubled. Cleansing or expiry ends the multiplier; changes already made remain.
